beats.intro: Chapter sixty-eight, the last chapter. [[sub]]A graph lets you see the solutions of a quadratic equation.
beats.idea: Compare the function y equals a x squared plus b x plus c with the equation a x squared plus b x plus c equals zero. [[zero]]The equation is the function with y replaced by zero. [[axis]]On the graph, y equals zero is the x-axis. [[ex]]So the solutions of the equation are the x-intercepts of the parabola. [[read]]For y equals negative two thirds x squared minus two thirds x plus four, the parabola crosses at negative three and two. [[chk]]Check one: at x equals two, negative eight thirds minus four thirds plus four is zero.
beats.count: The graph also shows how many solutions there are. [[two]]Two crossings, two solutions. [[one]]If the vertex just touches the axis, like two thirds times x plus two, squared, there's one solution: negative two. [[none]]If the parabola stays above or below the axis, like y equals x squared minus three x plus four, there is no real solution.
beats.q1: Quick check. Click a solution on the graph.
beats.sym: Symmetry helps too. [[given]]Suppose the vertex is at negative four, negative three, and one root is negative six. [[axis]]The axis of symmetry passes through the vertex, at x equals negative four. [[dist]]Negative six is two units to its left. [[mirror]]The other root is the same distance on the other side: two units to the right, at negative two.
beats.q2: Quick check. Find the other root.
beats.ball: Here's a real situation. [[kick]]A ball is kicked, and its height is y equals negative two x squared plus nine x, where x is the distance in meters. [[ground]]It hits the ground when the height is zero. [[fac]]Factor: x times negative two x plus nine equals zero. [[two]]So x is zero or four and a half. [[mean]]x equals zero is where it was kicked, so the ball lands four and a half meters away.
beats.approx: Not every graph crosses at a whole number. [[ex]]y equals x squared minus two x minus four crosses the x-axis between three and four, and between negative two and negative one. [[est]]The graph gives an estimate: about three point two, and about negative one point two. [[exact]]For exact values, use the quadratic formula: one plus or minus root five.
beats.q3: Quick check. Where does the cannonball land?
beats.wrap: To sum up. [[w1]]The solutions of a x squared plus b x plus c equals zero are the x-intercepts of y equals a x squared plus b x plus c. [[w2]]Two crossings, one touch, or none tell you how many real solutions there are. [[w3]]Roots sit symmetrically about the axis of symmetry. [[w4]]A graph can estimate a solution; algebra makes it exact. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice, the last one in the book.
beats.final1: Chapter practice. Read the solutions from the graph.
beats.final2: Next, solve and check with the graph.
beats.final3: Last one. Symmetry and a real situation.
beats.finish: Congratulations. That's the end of chapter sixty-eight, and the end of the book. You've come a long way, from types of numbers to quadratic functions.
